sentences.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission issued an interim report on electorate allowance risks, using a former parliamentarian's expenditure as a case study.
sentences.support: This interim report concerns the conduct of a former public officer, primarily as an illustration of the misconduct risk

sentences.text: The Commission considered unclear spending rules and absent controls a significant risk, but could not determine whether private misuse of allowances was widespread.
sentences.support: The vagueness of the allowance coupled with the lack of any controls represents a significant misconduct risk to the State

sentences.text: The Commission formed an opinion of serious misconduct concerning the former member's use of allowances for private purposes and claims for tax deductions.
sentences.support: In respect of Mr Edman's conduct as a public officer relating to his parliamentary allowances, the Commission has formed an opinion of serious misconduct.

sentences.text: The Commission stressed that this opinion did not establish guilt of an offence and that its investigation was continuing.
sentences.support: An opinion of serious misconduct is not, and is not to be taken as, a finding that a person has committed or is guilty of an offence.

sentences.text: The Commission suggested that the Salaries and Allowances Tribunal clarify the relationship between salary and allowances and make permitted spending more explicit.
sentences.support: The Commission also suggests that SAT consider reviewing the electorate allowance determination to make permitted and non-permitted expenditure more explicit.

notes: INTRODUCTION gives the purpose and interim status. The existing OPAX finding is not duplicated. Suggestions to the tribunal are described as suggestions rather than numbered formal recommendations.
